content.title: Trees and Urban Forestry
content.summary: The City of Arvada has declared Stage 1 drought water restrictions effective April 15, 2026, aiming to reduce water use by at least 20%. The city's Forestry Team has inventoried over 14,000 trees across various public properties, emphasizing the importance of trees in urban infrastructure and ecosystems. Residents can report trees overhanging power lines to Xcel Energy and are encouraged to utilize the city's free mulch pick-up site available from April to October.
content.body:
### [Updates](/CivicAlerts.aspx?CID=1)

1. #### [Stage 1 Drought Water Restrictions](/1499)

   The City has declared a drought and Stage 1 water restrictions are in effect beginning April 15, 2026. Stage 1 drought conditions mean water supply is low and mandatory restrictions are in place. The goal is to reduce water use by at least 20%. [Read on...](/1499)

[View All](/CivicAlerts.aspx?CID=1)

/CivicAlerts.aspx

Trees are a major part of the City's infrastructure, providing beauty while supporting vital ecosystems. More than 14,000 trees on the City of Arvada property have been inventoried by the City's Forestry Team. This number represents all the trees planted in Parks, Athletic Fields, City Facilities, roadways, and many of the trees located in our Open Space Areas.

**To report trees overhanging power lines, please contact Xcel Energy at 800-895-4999.**

Visit [Xcel Energy's website](https://co.my.xcelenergy.com/customersupport/s/trees) for more information regarding its vegetation management.

### [Tree FAQs](/Faq.aspx?TID=62)

[My trees are overhanging City property - is the City allowed to trim them?](#)
:   Yes, the City is allowed to trim resident-owned trees to our property line.

[City-owned trees are overhanging my property - can I trim them myself?](#)
:   Yes, you may trim City-owned trees to your property line.

[What should I expect if Xcel Energy is trimming trees on my property?](#)
:   Xcel Energy conducts routine vegetation management to maintain safe clearance between trees and power lines. If your property is scheduled for tree trimming, you may receive advance notice from Xcel or see crews working in your area.

    Xcel's contractors will trim branches that pose a risk to power lines. Small limbs and brush are typically hauled away, though some brush may be left curbside for pickup within a few days. Larger pieces of wood are cut into manageable lengths and left on your property for your use.

    For specific questions about Xcel's tree trimming practices, timing, or what to expect on your property, visit [Xcel's tree management resources](https://co.my.xcelenergy.com/customersupport/s/trees) or contact Xcel directly at 800-895-4999.

    Xcel's tree management resources has a list of FAQs that includes information about its [tree pruning methods](https://co.my.xcelenergy.com/customersupport/s/article/Can-you-top-or-prune-the-whole-tree-to-give-it-more-symmetrical-shape).

[I live near a trail (or open space/park) - when should I expect to see parks staff pruning the trees in these areas?](#)
:   With more than 30,000 trees on City property, maintaining them properly is a labor-intensive task. Pruning and other tree maintenance can be expected year around.

[Does the City provide free mulch?](#)
:   The City has a free mulch pick-up site at [the entrance to the Arvada-Blunn Reservoir (18915 W. 64th Ave)](https://www.google.com/maps/search/39.817149,+-105.213364?coh=219815&entry=tts&g_ep=EgoyMDI0MDYxMi4wKgBIAVAD).

    The mulch pick-up site is available seven days a week from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. from April 1 through October 31.

    Mulch is available on a first come, first served basis. Availability is not guaranteed. Mulch is intended for Arvada residents only.

    [![Map showing the City's  mulch pick-up site is located just east of Highway 93 off W. 64th Ave.](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4185)](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=4185)

[I live adjacent to a ditch - who is responsible for the tree maintenance of the area?](#)
:   If you are an adjacent landowner, the vegetation (including trees) along the ditch is your responsibility. Neither ditch companies nor municipalities generally own the land under and along the ditch. Instead, they have prescriptive easements, which allow them to dictate the use of the land within the easement. The ditch companies prioritize the removal of trees and vegetation that impede water flow. The rest is up to you. For more information about ditches, [visit our Ditches page for more information](/512/Ditches).

[View All](/Faq.aspx?TID=62)

## Free mulch pick-up site for Arvada residents

The City has a free mulch pick-up site [at the entrance to the Arvada-Blunn Reservoir (18915 W. 64th Ave)](https://maps.app.goo.gl/XpFpHSmymiJYdqCFA).

- The mulch pick-up site is available April 1 through October 31.
- The pick-up site is open seven days a week from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
- The mulch is free of charge and intended for Arvada residents only.
- Mulch is available on a first come, first served basis.
- Availability is not guaranteed.
- Residents are responsible for loading and hauling their own mulch.
- Click on the map below for an enlarged version.

[![Map showing the City's  mulch pick-up site is located just east of Highway 93 off W. 64th Ave.](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4185)](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=4185)![Free mulch pick-up site ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4190)

## City Forester Ian MacDonald featured on Inside Arvada podcast

City Forester Ian MacDonald was a guest on the City of Arvada's podcast, Inside Arvada. Ian talked about a variety of tree-related topics, including how Arvada earns its Tree City USA designation, what kinds of trees do best in Arvada's climate, the City's annual Arbor Day tree planting celebration and much more. Listen to the podcast using the player below or wherever you listen to podcasts, including [Apple](https://ow.ly/RbBu50RHquX), [Spotify](https://ow.ly/OcEw50RHquZ), [YouTube](https://youtu.be/5rA0DRNMfB4?feature=shared) and [Buzzsprout](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/episodes/15034665) (with transcript).

[![three city employees pose for a photo after recording a podcast ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4011)](https://www.buzzsprout.com/2320363/15034665)

## Emerald Ash Borer

For resources regarding EAB in Arvada, [visit the Emerald Ash Borer page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/727/Emerald-Ash-Borer-Alert).

## Trees on City Property

Our goal is to help promote and preserve Arvada's urban forest. Learn about the City's approach to the [general care, planting, and removal of trees on City property](/737/Trees-on-City-Property).

## Christmas Tree Recycling

Each year the City offers [free Christmas tree recycling](/717) for Arvada residents at Stenger Sports Complex. Mulch is made available free of charge at the drop-off site while supplies last during the collection period.

## Arbor Day Tree Planting

Each spring, the City Parks Department teams up with an Arvada elementary school to celebrate Arbor Day by planting trees together at a nearby park. The tradition began with Peck Elementary School and continued for 37 years. The annual tree planting is part of Arvada earning its Tree City USA designation from the Arbor Day Foundation each year.

Visit the [Arbor Day tree planting page](/724) to learn more about the most recent celebration!

## Plant-A-Tree Program

For information regarding the City's Plant-a-Tree program, [visit the Plant-A-Tree Program](/730/Plant-A-Tree-Program). (The Plant-A-Tree program runs from the **beginning of May through the end of****September**.)

## Trees Across Arvada

Each year the City of Arvada partners with the Colorado Tree Coalition's Trees Across Arvada Program to bring tree saplings to Arvada residents at a reduced cost. [Learn more on the Trees Across Arvada page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/733/Trees-Across-Arvada).

## Contact

Parks Maintenance 720-898-7410 or request information/service regarding City trees through [Ask Arvada](https://seeclickfix.com/web_portal/m96AzqbgQ9RW9z5CcqFqEwP8/issues/map).
